name: Robot Price Index
description: Price index for humanoid robots, quadruped robots, industrial arms and service robots. Every price carries an as-of date; estimates are labeled in price_note, never presented as offers.
license: CC BY 4.0 — free to use with a visible link to https://robotpriceindex.com

robots.price_note: Official base configuration (23 DoF) at $13,500 in Unitree's store; EDU configurations through US resellers run $43,900–73,900 across 12 variants.
robots.sdk: unitree_sdk2 (Python/C++), ROS 2 — EDU versions only; base G1 not programmable

robots.price_note: Unitree cut the R1's China-market starting price from 39,900 to 29,900 CNY (~$4,150) in June 2026, with immediate in-stock delivery. Global retail via AliExpress still runs $4,900 (R1 AIR) to $5,900 (R1); US-fulfilled listings are priced higher. Still the cheapest full humanoid on open sale; SDK-enabled EDU versions cost more.
robots.sdk: No SDK on R1/R1 AIR (not programmable); R1 EDU adds unitree_sdk2 (Python/C++, ROS 2)

robots.price_note: H1 listed at $90,000 in Unitree's store ("contact us for real price"); resellers quote $100k–129k. H1-2 with hands sold for $148,235 and was delisted in 2026 as the H2 ($29,900) replaces the line.
robots.sdk: unitree_sdk2 (Python/C++), ROS 2 via unitree_ros2

robots.price_note: Official retail at 88,000 CNY (~$12,000) for the business and education versions.
robots.sdk: Open platform: ROS support, open training code (Isaac Sim, MuJoCo, ONNX)

robots.price_note: Base price ~$22,000 in China; US resellers run $29,800 (Basic) to ~$50,925 (Standard with grippers), EU from €39,000 incl. tax. Open-source developer platform, RoboCup 2025 champion.
robots.sdk: Fully open-source SDK, ROS 2, Isaac Sim / Webots / MuJoCo simulation support

robots.price_note: Official pre-order: $20,000 Early Access ($200 deposit, US-only 2026 delivery) or a $499/month subscription with later delivery. Learns household tasks partly via teleoperation; international expansion from 2027.
robots.sdk: Closed consumer platform; app-controlled with teleoperation-assisted learning, no public SDK

robots.price_note: Channel pricing diverges: distributors list the GR-3 Care-Bot from ~$27,500 with final pricing on request, while other catalog listings cite $80,000. Care robot for homes and assisted living, in production since its CES 2026 debut.
robots.sdk: SDK and technical docs for approved research partners only

robots.price_note: A2 Lite at $44,560 in Agibot's own store (verified July 2026); the full bipedal A2 runs $100k–190k depending on configuration. 10,000 robots produced by March 2026.
robots.sdk: SDK + APIs; open-source AimRT middleware framework

robots.price_note: Wheeled humanoid. The 630,000 CNY (~$87k) model sold out on JD.com after the 2026 Spring Festival Gala; pharmacy deployments run ~700,000 CNY (~$96k). Price varies heavily with configuration and service.
Distributor catalog pricing: Adam SP at $100,000, Adam Lite at $120,000; final pricing on request. Modular quasi-direct-drive actuators up to 360 N·m, open-source SDK.
robots.sdk: Open-source SDK with low-level access; NVIDIA Isaac Gym training support

robots.price_note: No public list price — enterprise sales only. Estimates run $68k–120k per unit at small volumes (early adopters ~$90k), some sources up to $160k. Mass production underway with an order book over 800M CNY; swaps its own battery in 3 minutes.
robots.sdk: Closed, enterprise deployments only (BrainNet / Co-Agent stack)

robots.price_note: No sticker price — Digit is sold through robots-as-a-service contracts bundling hardware, Arc cloud software, workcell and support; the June 2026 investor deck models ~$8,500/month (~$100k/year) against a ~$30/hour labor benchmark. The widely cited ~$250,000 reflects Digit's real early purchase price and estimates in current pilot programs, marking the realistic upper bound for outright acquisition.
robots.sdk: Closed platform; Agility Arc cloud orchestration + enterprise APIs

robots.price_note: Estimated at $150,000+ — not officially published, enterprise sales only, no North American channel. Full-size 175 cm research and service platform with 12-DoF hands.
robots.sdk: SDK with ROS compatibility; developer platform actively maintained

robots.price_note: Kepler's stated target retail range of $20k–30k; no open price list, sales are corporate. Fifth-generation Forerunner with a 2.33 kWh battery rated for ~8 hours.

No public price. The widely quoted $20,000 is a stated consumer target, not an offer: there is no pre-order or retail channel, and all units go to internal programs and partner deployments (BMW Spartanburg). Enterprise pricing is negotiated.
robots.sdk: Closed — Helix VLA stack, no public SDK; internal and partner deployments only

robots.price_note: Tesla has never published a price for Optimus and has no order, reservation, waitlist or lease channel: as of August 2026 tesla.com carries no Optimus product page at all, only a recruiting page. The widely quoted $20,000-$30,000 is Elon Musk's long-term target at volume, stated in 2024, not a price - on Tesla's Q4 2024 earnings call he explicitly declined to name one, saying the price "will be set by market demand". On the Q1 2026 call he said Optimus would probably become useful outside Tesla "sometime next year", and Tesla's Q2 2026 10-Q reports no Optimus revenue. Any site taking Optimus pre-orders or deposits is not affiliated with Tesla.
robots.sdk: Closed, internal Tesla use only; no SDK or developer access

robots.price_note: Not publicly sold, no MSRP — analyst estimates run ~$130k–320k (some up to ~$420k). The production electric Atlas debuted at CES 2026 and the entire 2026 output is contracted (Hyundai Metaplant, Google DeepMind); Hyundai targets 30,000 units/year by 2028.
robots.sdk: Closed; partner deployments only (Hyundai, Google DeepMind), no public SDK

robots.price_note: Official retail by version: Air $1,600, Pro $2,800, Go2 X $4,500; EDU Standard $11,190, EDU Plus $13,205, top EDU configurations up to $19,430. Unitree cut prices across the line in 2026 ahead of its IPO.
robots.sdk: unitree_sdk2 (C++/Python), ROS 2 support

robots.price_note: Launched at 12,999 CNY (~$1,800) in Xiaomi's Chinese retail, still sold there with no successor; international resellers charge ~$3,000.
robots.sdk: Open-source SDK, ROS 2, graphical programming

robots.price_note: Dealer range by configuration: from $2,890 minimum listing / Basic RC $5,400, Venture $9,500, Pro $12,999, LiDAR version $18,900. Research platform.
robots.sdk: ROS 1 / ROS 2 SDK and motion APIs

robots.price_note: Dealer guide prices: ~$65,000 for the X30, ~$74,800 for the X30 Pro; some dealers quote on request only. Industrial IP67 quadruped for autonomous inspection.
robots.sdk: Open SDK for secondary development, ROS support

robots.price_note: Officially quote-only; US resellers list ~$76,900 (down from $85,900) for the base industrial configuration; full setups with LiDAR, sensors and software run substantially higher. The $12k figure floating around is not confirmed by any reseller.
robots.sdk: unitree_sdk2 (C++/Python), ROS 2 support

robots.price_note: The historical ~$74,500 Explorer Kit is no longer published — since 2026 sales are quota-based; real configurations in public procurement records run $150k–375k (Spot Arm, LiDAR and autonomy software add $25k+). Over 1,500 units deployed.
robots.sdk: Spot SDK (Python), gRPC API

robots.price_note: Channel pricing diverges: some resellers quote the CR5 at $10k–20k, while a major US reseller lists the CR5 from $22,980 and the updated CR5A from $24,320. RaaS subscription available. 5 kg payload cobot.
robots.sdk: TCP/IP SDK (Python, C++, ROS), DobotStudio Pro

robots.price_note: Estimated $12k–18k — JAKA positions itself 30–40% below Universal Robots at comparable specs. Indian dealer listings at ₹14.5–19.5 lakh (~$17.5k–23.4k) mark the upper bound with local markups. 7 kg payload cobot.
robots.sdk: JAKA App graphical programming, TCP/IP SDK, ROS adapter

robots.price_note: Guide price for arm + controller (FANUC sells via quotes, no public list): $17,500–20,000 typical, the /4S variant from ~$25,000. A fully deployed cell runs $45k–65k.
robots.sdk: R-30iB controller, KAREL, ROBOGUIDE

robots.price_note: Guide price for base hardware (KUKA sells via quotes): the KR AGILUS line starts around $25k; integration, tooling and software add $10k–50k.
robots.sdk: KRL (KUKA Robot Language), ROS-Industrial support

robots.price_note: Distributor guide (UR publishes no list price): arm + controller $32k–38k, typical 2026 US quotes $35k–48k; one concrete US listing at $37,245. A full cell with gripper and integration runs ~$60k.
robots.sdk: PolyScope, URCap ecosystem, URScript

robots.price_note: Legacy stock rather than a current product: the ER6 no longer appears anywhere in Estun's own ER-series catalog, whose small-payload slots are now filled by the ER3, ER4, ER7, ER8 and ER10 families. The ER6-1600 survives on distributor and marketplace listings and in an archived 2020 Estun catalog, so any price quoted for it today is for remaining stock through third parties, not a factory offer. Estun publishes no list price for this model.

Launch pricing: $7,999 outright or $449/month subscription; deliveries promised for fall 2026. Wheeled base with a height-adjustable torso (91–175 cm) rather than legs, which is how it undercuts bipedal home humanoids on price.
robots.sdk: Closed consumer platform; teleoperation-assisted autonomy, no public SDK

robots.price_note: The base H2 lists at $29,900 on the manufacturer's international store (out of stock as of mid-2026), while US resellers list it from $40,900 and the EDU edition from $68,900. The upper bound reflects the H2 Plus variant, reported at roughly $100,000 in press coverage. Store listing and reseller prices are firm offers; the H2 Plus figure is a reported price, not a public cart listing.
robots.sdk: Unitree SDK2 (C++/Python), ROS 2 support; NVIDIA Jetson AGX Thor option on EDU

robots.price_note: Apptronik has never published a price and Apollo cannot be purchased today; it is deployed only through enterprise pilot agreements (Mercedes-Benz, GXO, Jabil) arranged on a quote basis. The widely circulated $50,000 figure is a long-term at-scale cost target stated by the CEO in 2023, not a sale price. Apptronik points to Apollo 3 as its first true commercial product, targeted at 2027.
robots.sdk: Closed platform; enterprise integrations (NVIDIA GR00T partner), no public SDK

robots.price_note: No official price exists; XPENG's CEO has only said Iron could eventually cost 'similar to car prices'. Press reports circulate an estimate of around $150,000, which is an analyst/press estimate, not an offer. Mass production began in 2026 with first commercial deployments targeted for 2027; there are no public orders open.
robots.sdk: Closed; proprietary Turing AI chips (2,250 TOPS), no public SDK

robots.price_note: Launched at 199,000 yuan (about $27,500) in China with pre-orders open since early 2025; a US reseller lists it at $27,530, closely matching the manufacturer's price. Both figures are actual listed prices, not estimates. Positioned as one of the cheapest full-size dexterous humanoids on the market.
robots.sdk: Dobot ROM-1 robot operator model, programming interface included; 1500 TOPS edge compute

robots.price_note: The manufacturer's US store lists the xArm 6 at $9,500 (down from $11,000), while US resellers list it up to $10,499; both are live offer prices. The wider xArm line spans the xArm 5 at $5,799, the Lite 6 at $3,349, and the xArm 7 at $10,499 on the manufacturer's store. Bundle options with grippers and camera kits cost more.
robots.sdk: Python/C++ SDK, ROS/ROS 2, UFACTORY Studio GUI

robots.price_note: The manufacturer's store lists the 280 line from $599 (Arduino) through $649 (M5Stack) and $799 (Raspberry Pi) to $849 (Jetson Nano); all are live offer prices. European distributor listings run higher, around EUR 735-905 depending on variant. A desktop-class educational cobot rather than an industrial workhorse: 250 g payload, 280 mm working radius.
robots.sdk: Python, C++, C#, JS, ROS, myBlockly/myStudio; open-source GitHub ecosystem

robots.price_note: ABB sells through distributors on a quote basis with no public list price; the $30,000-38,000 range is an estimate drawn from distributor listings and industry cost guides for the base GoFa 5 configuration with controller. The family also includes GoFa 10 and GoFa 12 variants (up to 12 kg payload, 1.62 m reach) at higher price points. Treat the range as indicative, not an offer.
robots.sdk: ABB RobotStudio, Wizard Easy Programming, RAPID

robots.price_note: Yaskawa publishes no list price and sells via integrators and distributors on quotation; industry pricing guides and distributor listings place HC-series cobots in a $25,000-50,000+ band depending on controller and options, with the HC10DTP typically toward the middle of that range. This is an estimate, not an offer. IP67-rated and hand-guided teachable, aimed at damp or splash-prone industrial environments.
robots.sdk: Smart Pendant / hand-guided teaching, MotoPlus SDK, ROS driver

robots.price_note: ANYbotics does not publish a retail price; ANYmal is sold as a configured enterprise deployment (robot, docking, software, onboarding, support). Press reports and industry estimates place a unit at roughly $150,000-200,000, with the Ex-proof ANYmal X at the top of that range and total cost of ownership substantially higher. Treat all figures as estimates, not offers.
robots.sdk: ANYmal API and workforce/inspection software suite; enterprise integration, no consumer SDK

robots.price_note: Vision 60 is sold to government, defense and select enterprise customers only and is not available for civilian retail purchase. Press reports and procurement records put the per-unit price at roughly $150,000-165,000 in US deals, while a UK defense purchase valued two units with a warranty package at about $590,000 for the pair. All figures come from procurement disclosures, not a public price list.
robots.sdk: C/C++, ROS/ROS 2, MAVLink-compatible APIs, ATAK integration; physics-based simulator

robots.price_note: US resellers list BellaBot at around $15,900, with the upgraded BellaBot Pro at about $16,000; street-price estimates for base configurations start near $13,000. RaaS leases run from roughly $335/month on 36-month terms through US integrators. Final pricing is quote-based and varies with tray configuration and support package.
robots.sdk: Closed

robots.price_note: US reseller listings put the CC1 Pro at $24,000 and the CC1 Standard Edition at $31,250, with RaaS plans from about $479-917/month depending on edition and term. Manufacturer pricing is quote-based per configuration; installation, mapping and a 1-year warranty are typically bundled. Distributor prices outside the US start lower, around $14,000-15,000.
robots.sdk: Closed

robots.price_note: US reseller pricing starts at $13,500 with RaaS from about $542/month, while other US and EU distributor listings range from roughly $17,900 to $23,000 (about EUR 15,000 ex-VAT in Europe). The spread reflects regional distribution, the 23.8-inch ad screen configuration and bundled service. The manufacturer sells through channel partners with quote-based pricing.
robots.sdk: Closed

robots.price_note: US distributor listings range from $19,000-19,600 up to $28,600 depending on reseller and bundled elevator/door integration. Rental programs start around $575-650/month with short minimum terms. The W3 is Keenon's hotel-focused unit with four sealed compartments and multi-floor elevator access, which drives integration costs above list price.
robots.sdk: Closed

robots.price_note: US resellers list Servi Plus at $13,990 to buy, with financing from about $293/month and full-service RaaS leases from roughly $599/month (36-month) to $1,199/month (12-month) including installation, mapping and support. Bear Robotics primarily pushes the subscription model, and lease plans bundle software updates and service. A 28-day demo subscription is offered for a small installation fee.
robots.sdk: Closed

robots.price_note: US distributor listings price the base LuckiBot at $8,999, making it one of the cheapest branded delivery robots on the market. Upgraded variants are listed at $14,999 (LuckiBot Pro) and $16,999 (Pro Autodoor with sealed compartments). The manufacturer sells via channel partners; volume pricing is quote-based.
robots.sdk: Closed

robots.price_note: US distributor listings range from $39,999 (discounted from a $51,600 list price) to about $43,000, typically including on-site installation. RaaS deployment is offered at around $1,795/month covering hardware, training and support. Press reports cite $20,000-35,000 for base non-Pro configurations sourced outside the US channel.
robots.sdk: Closed

robots.price_note: US reseller listings price the dual-arm ADAM beverage robot at $180,000, with event rentals from $15,000 per day. A disclosed 60-month lease of 25 units for $5.25M implies roughly $3,500 per unit per month on long-term contracts, and earlier press reports cited $50,000-70,000 for simpler configurations. Most deployments are structured as leases or revenue-share rather than outright purchase.
robots.sdk: Closed

robots.price_note: AgiBot does not list an official price on its own channels; distributor listings for the X1 developer kit start around $19,499 for research labs. Because the full hardware design is open-sourced, labs can also self-build from the published files at component cost. Treat the figure as a distributor offer rather than a manufacturer list price.
robots.sdk: Fully open-source: hardware CAD, PowerFlow actuator designs, firmware and a Linux/ROS 2 stack with the AimRT framework, all published on GitHub

robots.price_note: Fourier has not published an official list price for the N1; distributor listings range from roughly $16,000 for kit configurations to about $40,000 for complete platforms. The full hardware design, BOM, CAD files and assembly instructions are published, so developers can source parts and build independently. Figures are distributor offers, not a manufacturer list price.
robots.sdk: Fully open-source: complete hardware blueprints, published BOM, CAD, assembly instructions and base control software on GitHub (FSA 2.0 actuators)

robots.price_note: K-Scale published a headline price of $8,999 for the first 100 units and took $100 preorders through the manufacturer store. The company shut down in November 2025 after failing to raise funding, cancelled preorders and refunded deposits, so the robot can no longer be purchased. All hardware and software IP was released under open-source licenses on the way out, per press reports.
robots.sdk: Fully open-source: mechanical CAD, Rust-based K-OS operating system and sim-to-real ML stack on GitHub; entire IP open-sourced after the company wound down

robots.price_note: Not a commercial product: this is a published open design intended for self-assembly, so no assembled units are sold. The published BOM totals under $5,000 at U.S. market prices, using widely available e-commerce components and desktop-3D-printed cycloidal gearboxes. Cost figure refers to the published BOM, not a sale price.
robots.sdk: Fully open-source: 3D-printable hardware design, published BOM, embedded code and RL training/deployment framework on GitHub

robots.price_note: Astribot has not published an official list price for the S1. Distributor listings put research editions near $50,000 and commercial units around $70,000, while press reports estimate early commercial pricing up to roughly $100,000 or more. Commercial deliveries began in China in late 2025 with international rollout during 2026; treat the range as an estimate pending a formal offer.
robots.sdk: Proprietary DuoCore dual-system AI architecture with imitation-learning pipeline; enterprise developer access via Astribot

robots.price_note: Officially launched in August 2025 with base pricing from RMB 158,000 (about $21,800) per manufacturer announcement and press reports. Higher trims (EDU and above) with onboard NVIDIA Orin compute cost more; final configuration pricing comes via quotation. One of the few full-size humanoids with a published entry price.
robots.sdk: Open Python SDK with modular hardware/software architecture; supports teleoperation, imitation learning and onboard-LLM autonomy (NVIDIA Orin on EDU trims)

robots.price_note: MagicLab operates a contact-sales model and has not published official pricing for the Z1. Distributor listings quote the compact research/education model from about $52,800. Its full-size sibling MagicBot G1 appears in distributor listings near $119,800; treat all figures as reseller offers rather than manufacturer list prices.
robots.sdk: Developer platform for research and education with secondary-development support; optional 11-DOF dexterous hands, 3D LiDAR and voice interaction

robots.price_note: The TianGong Walker consumer/research edition opened for preorders in 2025 at RMB 299,000, roughly $41,000-43,000 depending on exchange rate, per press reports. The underlying Tien Kung platform is state-backed and open: robot description assets and engineering documentation are published for research and secondary development. Enterprise configurations are quoted separately.
robots.sdk: Open platform: published URDF/design assets and engineering docs (Tien Kung Open Source) plus the Huisi Kaiwu embodied-AI software platform

robots.price_note: EngineAI executives indicated a target price of RMB 150,000-200,000 (about $20,500-27,400) when global sales opened in late 2024, per press reports. Distributor listings for export configurations quote substantially higher, up to roughly $54,000. The spread reflects commercial vs education editions and regional markups.
robots.sdk: Developer SDK with commercial and education editions; end-to-end neural motion control (RL + imitation learning), 360-degree LiDAR and depth cameras

robots.price_note: Sanctuary AI has never published a price for Phoenix and does not sell units outright; the robot is deployed through enterprise pilot programs in manufacturing settings. Press reports place comparable research-grade humanoids in the six-figure range, but no official figure exists for Phoenix. Any specific number would be speculation.
robots.sdk: Proprietary Carbon AI cognitive control system (natural-language-to-action with auditable reasoning); no public SDK — hydraulic hands with 21 DOF and near-human tactile sensing

robots.price_note: Neura announced transparent pricing at CES 2026: the industrial 4NE1 Gen 3.5 lists at EUR 98,000 (about $105,000), dropping to around EUR 60,000 (about $65,000) at fleet scale, per press reports. A smaller 4NE1 Mini is offered at EUR 19,999 for home and research use. Gen 3.5 deliveries are slated for late 2026, so current orders are preorders.
robots.sdk: Neuraverse fleet-learning OS and app ecosystem; NVIDIA Thor compute with Isaac GR00T integration, modular exchangeable forearms and hands

robots.price_note: Pudu does not publicly disclose D9 pricing; units are quoted individually through the manufacturer and distributor listings on a request basis. No credible published figures exist as of August 2026, so the price is listed as unavailable rather than estimated. Pudu's commercial service-robot channel suggests enterprise-oriented sales.
robots.sdk: Proprietary stack with 275 TOPS onboard compute, real-time 3D semantic mapping and DH11 11-DOF tactile dexterous hands; developer access via Pudu

robots.price_note: The wheeled Go2-W is not sold on Unitree's consumer store; pricing comes from US resellers and distributor listings. Base configurations start around $13,999, while higher-tier Smart/Ultimate/Inspection and enterprise (ENT) builds run roughly $20,700-24,000. A mid-2026 price cut brought the top enterprise variant down to about $23,999.
robots.sdk: Unitree SDK2 / ROS 2

robots.price_note: US resellers list the industrial B2-W at roughly $88,900-100,000 depending on the sensor and compute configuration. European distributor listings start lower, from about EUR 58,800 before options. Unitree itself quotes B2-series pricing per project rather than publishing a list price.
robots.sdk: Unitree SDK2 / ROS 2

robots.price_note: The X20 has been superseded by the X30 ($75,000 at US distributor listings) and is labeled discontinued on the US site, though it remains on the global catalog. Press price guides cite roughly $20,000 for remaining X20 units; original enterprise deployments were quoted higher depending on LiDAR, thermal and 5G options. Treat this as an estimate - the manufacturer sells by quotation only.
robots.sdk: Deep Robotics SDK, ROS support

robots.price_note: US distributor listings price the wheel-legged Lynx M20S at $59,995 and the M20 Pro (dual 96-line LiDAR, autonomous charging) at about $61,200. These are offer prices for standard configurations; payload accessories and gimbals are extra. The M20 won a CES 2026 Innovation Award, and demand keeps street prices close to list.
robots.sdk: Deep Robotics SDK, ROS support

robots.price_note: No public price. Deep Robotics has not listed the S10, and its new Japan distributor ELSA quotes it by inquiry only. The S10 is a lighter wheel-legged sibling of the Lynx M20 (about $60,000 in US distributor listings) at roughly 40% less weight, so treat any number below that as a guess until a quote surfaces.
robots.sdk: Deep Robotics SDK, ROS support

robots.price_note: MiR sells exclusively through its distributor network on a request-a-quote basis, and US distributor listings show no public price for the MiR250. Final cost depends heavily on top modules (lifts, conveyors, hooks) and MiR Fleet licensing, so quoted deployments vary widely per site. No verified public figure exists as of August 2026.
robots.sdk: MiR Fleet software, REST API

robots.price_note: Locus does not sell Origin units outright - it is deployed under a Robots-as-a-Service model with hardware, LocusOne software, integration and support bundled into the subscription. Press reports place typical RaaS rates at roughly $2,000-4,000 per robot per month on 12-36 month terms. Equivalent hardware value is estimated by press at $25,000-50,000 per unit.
robots.sdk: LocusOne fleet platform

robots.price_note: Geek+ sells its goods-to-person P-series project-based, so no official list price exists for the flagship P1200R. Distributor listings for P-series units run from about $35,000 for the mid-range P800R up to the mid-$60,000s, with the 1,200 kg P1200R at the upper end - treat the range as an estimate. Full system cost also includes the Geek+ RMS fleet software and workstations.
robots.sdk: Geek+ Robot Management System (RMS)

robots.price_note: AGILOX publishes no list price for the ONE, and neither do its distributors: the Swiss dealer webshop renders the price as "EUR --,--" behind a registration wall, and the DACH, Nordic and US resellers are all quote-only. AGILOX does publish the structure of its rental offer - a fixed base fee plus a variable fee per operating hour over 12-60 months, alongside short-term rent of 1-12 months and leasing through partners - but discloses no rate for any of them. No published price, rental rate or procurement figure for the ONE exists as of August 2026.
robots.sdk: AGILOX X-Swarm intelligence

robots.price_note: US resellers list the industrial T300 at $20,990 for outright purchase, with the lifting variant priced separately. Pudu and its partners also offer the robot under Robot-as-a-Service subscription terms. This is one of the few industrial-payload AMRs with a public sticker price.
robots.sdk: PUDU Cloud / Open API

robots.price_note: German Bionic does not publish a list price for the Apogee; press reports cite $9,900 for the closely related Apogee+ variant, which is the best public anchor. Most corporate deployments run on rental terms of roughly GBP 350 per unit per month plus a one-off vest purchase. The newer Apogee ULTRA (36 kg support) is in preorder with undisclosed pricing. Provides up to 30 kg of active lifting support.
robots.sdk: Closed (German Bionic IO)

robots.price_note: The manufacturer's own web store lists the Ekso EVO upper-body vest at $1,495, with Level 2 support springs included and other spring levels sold separately. This is far below the roughly $7,000 press-reported price of its EksoVest predecessor. Passive spring assist of 2.2-6.8 kg per arm for overhead work; no battery required.

Press reports cite a list price of EUR 5,900 (about $6,400) for the passive Paexo Back, with leasing from EUR 69 per month via the manufacturer. Purely mechanical design that relieves the lower back by up to 25 kg during lifting, with no battery or charging. Sold through Ottobock's industrial (Bionic Exoskeletons) channel and distributors.

The manufacturer publishes pricing openly: $1,999 per individually fitted suit for single users, dropping to about $1,499 per suit in corporate volume packages (e.g. $14,990 for 10 users). Enterprise deployments can use Exo-as-a-Service from under $99 per user per month, and a $4,999 all-sizes research kit is offered to institutions. Passive textile exosuit with a mechanical on/off clutch that cuts back muscle strain by 20-40%.

Not for sale: BYD has disclosed no price, no order channel and no production timeline. Xiao Di debuted as a working prototype in early August 2026 at BYD's Di Space showroom in Zhengzhou, where the company plans to place two to three units per dealership as a greeter that explains vehicles to customers. BYD has not said whether the robot will ever be sold to third parties.

AgiBot publishes no price for the A2 Ultra: its own store lists the robot as contact-sales only, and units are supplied through enterprise agreements. Figures circulating for this class of robot are analyst estimates rather than quoted offers, so none is shown here.
robots.sdk: AimMaster control client; Linksoul platform for enterprise task customization. No open public SDK terms published.

robots.price_note: Fourier never announced a price for the GR-1; production units went quote-only to research institutions and industrial partners. Mass-production unit costs of roughly $150,000-$170,000 have appeared in press reports, but those are reported cost estimates, not a purchasable price. As of 2026 the GR-1 is no longer in Fourier's lineup, which has moved on to the GR-2 and GR-3.

Figure AI never published an MSRP for Figure 02 and sells it through no store or configurator; the robot was deployed only through commercial partnerships and pilots such as the BMW line. Per-unit figures around $130,000 in press reports are estimates of pilot cost, not a quoted price. Figure 02 has since been superseded by Figure 03.

Leju has not published a unit price for KUAVO; research-edition units are quoted directly to universities, labs and industrial customers. Chinese press describes early deliveries as costing several hundred thousand yuan each, but that is commentary rather than a listed offer, so no price is shown.
robots.sdk: Open developer stack: public source repository (kuavo_opensource), SDK, documentation, simulation platform and 20+ demo cases; open embodied-AI manipulation datasets.

robots.price_note: ROBOTERA has not published a price for STAR1 and offers no purchase channel; the robot was presented as a high-speed locomotion demonstrator, best known for its Gobi Desert running record. Per-unit figures near $50,000 and $120,000 appear in secondary reports, but they conflict and none traces to a manufacturer announcement, so both are treated as estimates.

Rainbow Robotics announced pre-order pricing itself: $80,000 for the research platform and $120,000 for the commercial platform, VAT excluded, with deliveries from October 2024. The price excludes the optional high-performance 3D recognition sensor and the Master ARM teaching kit; ordering runs through the manufacturer's sales team. This is a wheeled bimanual mobile manipulator rather than a biped.
robots.sdk: rby1-sdk - official Python and C++ SDK, Apache 2.0, on GitHub

robots.price_note: NEURA lists the Mini on its own reservation store at EUR 19,999 (Standard) and EUR 29,999 (Pro), about $23,100 to $34,650 at ~1.155 USD/EUR. A refundable EUR 100 reservation fee is credited against the purchase; the Pro premium buys 12-DoF dexterous hands, the C++ SDK, digital-twin access and teleoperation. Shipping was announced for April 2026; taxes, shipping and support contracts are excluded.
robots.sdk: Neuraverse OS with NVIDIA Isaac GR00T foundation models; C++ SDK, digital twin and teleoperation in the Pro tier

robots.price_note: No price and no sales channel. Mobileye, which agreed to acquire Mentee Robotics in January 2026, expects first on-site customer proof-of-concept deployments in 2026, with series production targeted for 2028. Older press figures around $35,000, and a roughly $20,000 future unit cost, are unconfirmed projections rather than offers, and Mobileye's own release quotes no per-unit number.

Clone Robotics publishes no price. Its own pre-order page invites reservations for a limited run of 279 units but states no unit price, no deposit and no delivery date. Figures circulating in press and forums run from about $20,000 to over $200,000 and none traces to the manufacturer. No complete Alpha has been publicly demonstrated walking unsupported as of August 2026.

AI2 Robotics publishes no list price and sells through enterprise contracts in China. A September 2025 order from a display manufacturer's subsidiary for more than 1,000 robots was reported at close to RMB 500 million, which implies roughly RMB 500,000 (about $69,000 at 7.2 RMB/USD) per unit - but that is an average across three years of deployment at multiple sites, not a purchasable price. A separate press report quoting 'from about $15,000' is unverified and irreconcilable with the order value, so no figure is published here.

US distributor listings quote $25,000 to buy the Whiz commercial vacuum outright, or robot-as-a-service from about $839/month on a 36-month term (up to ~$1,042/month on shorter terms). SoftBank Robotics itself publishes no price and sells by quote; the subscription bundles hardware, installation, training, software updates and support, while filters, dust bags, brushes and replacement batteries are extra.

PAL Robotics sells TIAGo by quote only, with no published list price. The only manufacturer-linked figures date from the 2015 launch (roughly EUR 30,000 base without arm, EUR 50,000 with a 7-DoF arm, EUR 60,000 with the five-fingered hand); those predate the current hardware by a decade and are not treated as a current price. Configuration - arm count, laser range, end-effector, AI kit, software packages - drives most of the cost.
robots.sdk: ROS (Ubuntu LTS, RT Preempt), MoveIt!, ros_control

robots.price_note: Reachy 2 launched at a publicly stated $70,000, quoted by Hugging Face's CEO and widely covered in the tech press after Hugging Face acquired Pollen Robotics in April 2025. Reduced configurations (stationary, single-arm) were quoted lower before launch. The price covers the robot platform; shipping, duties, spare parts and training are not included.
robots.sdk: Python SDK, ROS 2 Humble, LeRobot (open source)

robots.price_note: Hello Robot publishes an open list price of $24,950 for Stretch 3 on its own product site, in the standard configuration with dexterous wrist, gripper camera and second head camera. The maker has since introduced Stretch 4 at a published $29,950, so Stretch 3 is now the previous generation. Price excludes shipping, duties and optional end-effectors.
robots.sdk: ROS 2 and Python SDK (open source), Stretch AI

robots.price_note: Boston Dynamics has never published a price for Stretch; it has been sold by quote since commercial availability in 2022, and the announcement itself went out for a yet-to-be-named price. Figures of $300,000-$500,000 circulating online are third-party estimates rather than offers. Announced fleet deals (a $15M DHL Supply Chain pre-order, a $10M NFI order) cover many robots plus deployment and service and cannot be divided into a unit price.

European distributor listings put the LARA 5 at EUR 18,900 excl. VAT (about $21,800), with the wider family running EUR 16,500 for LARA 3 to EUR 26,900 for LARA 15 (roughly $19,100-$31,100). The price covers robot, control box and teach panel; gripper, tooling, integration and VAT are extra. NEURA itself quotes on request, and the distributor pages carrying these figures now show the products as unavailable - treat the numbers as a published anchor rather than a live offer.
robots.sdk: NeuraPy API, NR easy drag-and-drop GUI; EtherCAT/IO-Link, Ethernet/IP, PROFINET, Modbus TCP/RTU

robots.price_note: European distributor listings show MAiRA S at EUR 37,500 excl. VAT (about $43,300) and MAiRA M at EUR 39,500 (about $45,600); NEURA does not publish MAiRA pricing itself and sells on quotation. The figure excludes VAT, gripper, optional force-torque sensor, integration and support. The distributor pages carrying these figures now show the products as unavailable, so treat them as a published anchor rather than a live offer.
robots.sdk: Python NeuraPy API, NR easy GUI, optional low-level controller/sensor access; GPIO, Modbus TCP/RTU

robots.price_note: Shadow Robot published EUR 110,000 for the full 20-DoF Shadow Hand Plus, including shipping, installation, training and support (about $127,000); the same manufacturer post prices a cut-down 2-finger 7-DoF hand at about EUR 45,000. The figure comes from Shadow's own pricing article and has not been restated since, so treat it as an anchor rather than a live quote - the company sells on request.
robots.sdk: Full ROS integration (EtherCAT stack), Python/C++ API, Gazebo model; source and schematics under NDA

robots.price_note: Unitree lists no price for the A2 on its own site (contact sales); US reseller listings show A2 Standard at $31,900 and A2 Pro at $40,900, both currently out of stock. Prices cover the robot with dual batteries and exclude shipping, duties, the wheeled A2-W variant and expansion compute docks, which are quoted separately.
robots.sdk: Unitree secondary development (high- and low-level), ROS 2, NVIDIA Isaac Sim support

robots.price_note: Wandercraft publishes no list price. Atalante X is a medical device sold to rehabilitation institutions under contract, and in France through central public purchasing agencies with multi-year instalment options. Press reports around the US launch put European hospital units at roughly $176,000 each (about EUR 150,000) - a reported figure rather than a quoted price, and it says nothing about what training, service or financing are included.

Listed at $44,560 on AgiBot's own global online store, quoted directly in USD. The price covers the robot, battery pack, battery and accessory chargers, wireless e-stop, wireless controller and transport cart, with a 1-year / 3,000-hour warranty. Shipping is quoted separately at roughly $500-$3,000 depending on destination, and customs duties and taxes are the buyer's responsibility.
robots.sdk: AgiBot Botnet software support; motion development and swarm control tools

robots.price_note: LimX Dynamics' own store lists TRON 1 Standard Edition at $15,000 and the Education Edition at $25,000, both purchasable directly. The Standard package includes the robot body, three interchangeable foot modules (point-foot, sole, wheeled), battery, charging dock, handheld controller, haulage rope and roll cage; the SDK and secondary-development toolchain come only with the $25,000 Education Edition. Shipping, duties and dexterous hands or arms are not included.
robots.sdk: Python and C++ SDK with open hardware interface (Education Edition only)

robots.price_note: At the December 2025 launch LimX Dynamics stated $20,000 for the dual-arm EDU configuration and $25,000 for the full 3-in-1 EDU kit (dual-arm, bipedal and wheeled-leg modules); orders run through the manufacturer's consultation form rather than its self-serve store. US resellers list the 3-in-1 EDU kit substantially higher, around $33,000, with freight and customs quoted separately. Lower figures circulating for a stripped base configuration are unconfirmed and not used here.
robots.sdk: Python and C++; ROS 1 / ROS 2; Isaac Sim, MuJoCo and Gazebo simulation support

robots.price_note: Booster Robotics announced the K1 Geek Edition at $5,999 at its October 2025 launch, quoted in USD by the maker, with a $4,999 promotional price during the launch window only. The Geek price covers the 22-DoF robot with 48 TOPS compute, a 2Ah battery (about 30 minutes of runtime), carrying case and a 3-month warranty. The Education (117 TOPS) and Professional (200 TOPS) editions add a 5Ah battery and a 1-year warranty but carry no publicly listed price.
robots.sdk: Secondary development supported; upgradeable firmware, Gigabit Ethernet expansion

robots.price_note: Listed at $7,680 on AgiBot's own global online store, alongside the D1 Pro at $3,200 and D1 Edu at $6,080, quoted directly in USD. Shipping, customs duties and optional payload modules (LiDAR, depth camera, RTK, 4G/5G, video transmission) are not included.
robots.sdk: Secondary development supported, with an embedded reinforcement-learning locomotion stack

robots.price_note: Unitree's own store checkout prices the As2 Air at $3,100 and the As2 Pro at $4,650; the As2 EDU carries Unitree's $100,000 contact-sales placeholder rather than a real price and is excluded from this range. Prices exclude shipping, duties and optional sensor payloads, and the Air variant is currently backordered. Press reports quoting a higher entry price refer to industrial configurations.

Listed at $15,999 on Unitree's own store and marked ready to ship, with a further $1,000 per unit shipping charge stated on the product page. The higher-payload Z1 Pro variant is backordered and not separately priced there. End effectors beyond the standard gripper, duties and taxes are not included.
robots.sdk: C++/Python SDK over Ethernet with position and force control; Ubuntu host, ROS support

robots.price_note: Published at $29,950 on Hello Robot's own purchase page, up from $24,950 for Stretch 3. The price includes the compliant gripper, battery and ballast, wall power supply, Aruco tag kit, gamepad and pistol teleop controllers, tools and cables, with a 30-day return window and a 1-year warranty. Add-ons are priced separately: docking station $1,495, parallel gripper $1,495, NVIDIA Jetson Orin NX $2,495, spare battery and ballast $1,495, 3-year extended warranty $2,495. Typical lead time is 2-4 weeks.
robots.sdk: Open-source ROS 2 and Python SDK; 3D SLAM navigation and data-collection tooling

robots.price_note: Preorders open on JD.com (official channel) with a 3,000 CNY deposit: 119,800 CNY (~$16,500) for the semi-torso U1 Lite, up to 880,000/990,000 CNY (~$121,000/$136,500) for the flagship full-body U1 Ultra (female/male). A mid-tier U1 Pro is also listed without a confirmed public price. Over 13,000 units reserved as of the June 30, 2026 launch event; first deliveries due no later than September 15, 2026, so nobody has one in hand yet.

Authorized US resellers publish an outright purchase price of $13,995-$14,000, covering the robot, first-year software and a one-year warranty; freight, on-site mapping and staff training are quoted separately. The same resellers offer it on subscription from $395/month.

US distributor listings run from $6,500 for a base configuration to a $12,999 quoted MSRP, with $10,000 the most common published figure; the price covers the robot, standard trays and first-year software, but not freight, installation or site mapping. A subscription alternative is published from $270/month. The spread reflects configuration and dealer rather than a manufacturer list price - Pudu publishes none.

US distributor listings publish $15,000-$17,999 for outright purchase, the higher figure quoted as MSRP before freight and installation. Lease-to-own runs roughly $1,000-$1,250/month over 12-24 months. The price covers the four-tray robot, pager and charging dock; a spare hot-swap battery and elevator integration are extra.

Sold only on subscription - no outright purchase price is published. Relay Robotics' CEO has stated the subscription works out to about $75,000 over three years (roughly $2,080/month) with all maintenance and support included; earlier press reports put the lease near $2,000/month. Cost varies with the number of floors, elevator integrations and fleet size, so every deployment is quoted.

An authorized US reseller publishes $22,500 for outright purchase or $1,195/month on subscription, covering the robot, elevator-integration software and first-year support but not the building-side elevator controller work, which is quoted per property. Bear Robotics has since retired the model: its product page returns 404 and the Servi Lift is absent from the company's sitemap, so what remains is reseller stock.

LG publishes no MSRP; an authorized US reseller lists $17,900 for outright purchase or $746/month on subscription, covering the robot, software and first-year support but not freight, mapping or elevator integration. LG's own US business site currently returns no in-production ServeBot listings and marks the drawer-type LDLIM21 as discontinued, so availability should be confirmed before ordering.

Yunji's Hong Kong IPO prospectus discloses an actual 2024 average selling price of RMB 13,100 for the RUN delivery robot - about $1,820 at 7.2 RMB/USD - and Chinese retail listings have appeared around RMB 21,800 (~$3,030). The lower figure is a disclosed average realised price to hotel customers rather than a list price a buyer can take, so the range spans both. For context, the same filing puts the multi-function UP model at RMB 22,300 (~$3,100), and both prices fell sharply from RMB 23,200 and RMB 54,200 in 2022.

Sold only as robot-as-a-service at $5,400 per month with no upfront cost; the fee covers hardware, software, warranty, preventive maintenance and 24/7 bilingual support, while POS integration and extended analytics are paid add-ons. No outright purchase price has ever been published, so no purchase figure is shown here. For reference, the previous-generation Flippy 2 was offered at $3,500 per month plus an $11,000 installation fee.

Hyphen's CEO stated on the record in December 2025 that the automated makelines cost between $50,000 and $100,000 to buy, the spread depending on configuration, and that customers often reach payback in under a year. Leases and pilot deals are offered as an alternative to outright purchase. The stated range covers the unit itself and does not spell out kitchen retrofit, integration or ongoing service.

US distributor listings price the bare robot at $23,800, with the auto-charging dock a separate $1,000 accessory and the bundle with the enhanced workstation listed from $29,500. Subscription is offered from $989 per month on a 36-month term. Prices exclude sales tax, freight, installation, training and wear parts such as squeegees and brushes.

A US reseller lists the C30 at $12,200 including the 110V charging station and free domestic shipping; a European distributor lists the same machine at EUR 11,880 excluding VAT. Rental is offered from about $349 per month on a two-month minimum. Prices exclude VAT and duties, installation, training and consumables such as dust bags and mop pads.

Not for sale: Unitree unveiled this locomotion prototype on August 18, 2026, saying it was built in just over three months. The company disclosed a top running speed and a standing jump height but no price, no hands or end-effectors, no production timeline and no order channel — it says the machine remains a work in progress.

Manufacturer's own site lists the Nori A3 at $1,688 full price with no deposit, for a second, limited production batch shipping fall 2026. It is a consumer device controlled and trained through a laptop app rather than a turnkey enterprise deployment.
robots.sdk: Nori Lab (laptop app), Skills Marketplace
